evals.name: passive-feature-implementation
evals.prompt: Add a retry option to src/api/client.ts. The client already has requestJson<T>() and a typed ApiError. Keep the behavior easy to follow and add whatever tests make sense.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads maintainable-code passively, reads nearby code and tests before editing, keeps retry logic typed and localized, avoids broad abstraction, adds focused tests, and reports verification.

assertions.text: Uses existing local patterns before introducing new helpers
Keeps retry policy decomposed from HTTP transport only if the local codebase supports that boundary
Runs or identifies focused tests/typechecks

evals.name: decomposition-edge-case
evals.prompt: This 220-line function is hard to read. Split it up, but don't create a maze of tiny helpers. It mixes validation, database reads, pricing rules, and response formatting.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/decomposition.md, identifies stable responsibilities, preserves behavior with characterization tests where needed, and extracts helpers around validation, I/O, policy, and formatting only where boundaries improve readability.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/decomposition.md
Does not split solely by line count
Adds or recommends characterization coverage before risky refactoring

evals.name: review-finding-priority
evals.prompt: Review this PR for maintainability. The diff adds a generic RuleEngine class, removes three explicit functions, and has no tests for the new configuration format.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/review-rubric.md, leads with concrete findings ordered by severity, calls out abstraction and test risks with file/line evidence, and avoids nit-only review output.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/review-rubric.md
Findings are ordered by maintainer impact rather than style preference
Review cites concrete evidence instead of vague clean-code advice

evals.name: handoff-plan
evals.prompt: Write a plan another agent can execute to untangle billing calculation from the React checkout page. The executor will not have this conversation.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/implementation-plans.md and produces a self-contained plan with exact files, current-state evidence, local conventions, ordered steps, verification commands, done criteria, and stop conditions.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/implementation-plans.md
Plan is self-contained and does not refer to conversation context
Plan includes verification commands and stop conditions

evals.name: operational-code-comments
evals.prompt: Improve a GitHub Actions workflow step that fetches artifacts with gh api, filters them with jq, de-duplicates with sort -u, then downloads each artifact. Keep the script maintainable for a junior maintainer with good fundamentals.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/commenting.md, keeps the shell/YAML idiomatic, and adds useful phase comments explaining the artifact list fetch, prefix matching contract, de-duplication, empty-match guard, and GitHub API assumptions instead of narrating syntax.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/commenting.md
Adds developer comments for phase, data shape, external API contract, and failure handling
Does not add comments that merely restate shell syntax

evals.name: language-and-markup-comment-guidance
evals.prompt: Review comments in a TypeScript retry helper, a SQL migration CTE, and a CSS sticky command bar. Distinguish helpful maintainer comments from comments that just narrate syntax.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/commenting.md, evaluates comments across application code, database code, and UI markup, preserves comments that explain contracts or invariants, and recommends removing or replacing comments that merely restate syntax.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/commenting.md for non-CI code comment guidance
Differentiates syntax narration from invariant, tradeoff, data-shape, or layout-context comments
Covers at least one programming language and one markup or configuration language

evals.name: source-backed-method-property-comments
evals.prompt: Add maintainability comments to a Laravel model accessor, a typed TypeScript retry policy property, and a Next.js route handler. Include docblocks or comments wherever they help a junior maintainer, and link official sources for framework claims.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/commenting.md, places comments at method, property, and block level where useful, keeps explanations junior-friendly with bullets or numbered structure for multi-part concepts, verifies current official documentation for the actual language and framework claims in the prompt, and paraphrases source-backed behavior instead of inventing details.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/commenting.md
Adds comments or docblocks at method, property, and dense block levels instead of only class-level comments
Uses bullet or numbered structure for multi-concept comments intended for junior maintainers
Verifies and links official documentation for framework or language claims

evals.name: ascii-diagram-comment-guardrail
evals.prompt: Document a webhook processing function that validates payloads, enqueues accepted events, retries transient queue failures, and rejects malformed requests. Use comments or docblocks that a junior maintainer can scan quickly, including an ASCII diagram if it helps. The existing comment says malformed requests are retried, but the code now rejects them immediately.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/commenting.md, adds a compact ASCII flow diagram only if it clarifies the webhook path, makes the diagram labels match the actual validation/enqueue/retry/reject behavior, updates stale prose that conflicts with the code, and checks that arrows, branch labels, and surrounding text agree before finishing.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/commenting.md
Uses an ASCII diagram when it clarifies a non-obvious flow
Updates stale prose comments that conflict with the code or diagram
Verifies the ASCII diagram, prose, and code describe the same behavior

evals.name: negative-non-code
evals.prompt: Rewrite this launch announcement so it sounds more polished and concise.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not trigger because the task is non-code writing with no maintainability or software design surface.

assertions.text: Does not load maintainable-code or produce code maintainability guidance

evals.name: review-runtime-default-guardrails
evals.prompt: Review evals/files/runtime-defaults.ts before we use it in a mature service. We want stricter records eventually, no accidental external traffic in tests, and protection from destructive production commands. Propose the narrowest maintainable shape and a staged rollout; do not invent a general plugin framework.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the guardrails reference, identifies the inverted dangerous defaults and unconditional mutability, distinguishes configured/applicable/selected/applied state, proposes fail-closed test and production policies, stages strictness as a behavior migration, and keeps the orchestration direct.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/guardrails-and-quality-gates.md
Distinguishes configured policy, environment applicability, orchestration selection, and successfully applied effects
Makes destructive commands and unstubbed test network access fail closed
Replaces unconditional mutable dates with contract-appropriate immutable value semantics or explains why mutation is required
Treats strict-record adoption as a behavior migration backed by characterization or compatibility coverage
Does not create a generic registry or plugin system without independent policies that justify it

evals.name: design-executable-quality-gate
evals.prompt: Our Go module claims support for Go 1.23 and 1.24 plus the oldest and newest supported database-driver versions. CI currently runs only `go test ./...` on Go 1.24. Define a maintainable local check workflow and bounded CI matrix. The repository's formatter and rewrite tool both have write and check/diff modes.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes to guardrail guidance and proposes a non-mutating umbrella check that composes formatting, lint/type analysis, codemod dry-run, and behavior tests, while exercising the lowest and current supported combinations without turning CI into an unbounded matrix.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/guardrails-and-quality-gates.md
Separates formatter and codemod write modes from CI check or dry-run modes
Includes static or type analysis and behavior tests rather than treating one tool as the complete gate
Exercises lowest-supported and current runtime/dependency combinations with a bounded matrix
Provides one documented local check entry point that CI invokes or faithfully mirrors

evals.name: negative-disposable-shell-command
evals.prompt: Give me one disposable shell command that prints the top-level keys in config.json. Do not edit the repo or turn this into a script; I will throw the command away after running it once.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not trigger because this is an explicitly one-off shell command with no durable code or maintainability surface.

assertions.text: Does not load maintainable-code or introduce maintainability architecture, tests, comments, or quality gates

evals.name: coalesces-expensive-report-job
evals.prompt: I'm adding a Next.js endpoint at app/api/reports/monthly/route.ts that starts a background job to generate an account's monthly PDF report. Ten people from the same account may click Generate at once. Design the implementation and name the database fields, queue behavior, retries, and logs.
evals.expected_output: The response designs one durable work key per account/month, uses atomic uniqueness or upsert, returns an existing active job instead of enqueueing duplicates, includes lease/heartbeat/stale recovery, bounded retries, and structured logs with correlation ID and job key.

assertions.text: Uses a stable job or idempotency key to coalesce duplicate report generation.
Includes stale pending/running recovery and bounded retry behavior.
Mentions structured logs with correlation ID, work key, attempt, and outcome.

evals.name: handles-provider-timeout-after-side-effect
evals.prompt: Our Laravel app calls a payment provider from a queued CapturePayment job. Sometimes the provider times out after the charge may have succeeded. Explain how the job should retry, reconcile, and avoid double capture.
evals.expected_output: The response routes to distributed systems and job guidance, uses provider idempotency keys, classifies unknown timeout results as reconciliation before retry, aligns worker timeout below retry_after or visibility timeout, and records terminal or retryable states.

assertions.text: Treats timeout after side effect as unknown and requires reconciliation or same idempotency key.
Avoids retrying payment capture with a new idempotency key.
Mentions worker timeout and retry/visibility alignment.

evals.name: golden-signals-observability
evals.prompt: I'm adding logging and metrics around our image-processing worker. I don't want random log spam. What should we instrument and alert on?
evals.expected_output: The response makes latency, traffic, errors, and saturation the metrics baseline, then adds queue age, retries, stale jobs, dead letters, structured logs for state transitions, traces around async handoffs/provider calls, and alerts only on user impact or exhausted automation.

assertions.text: Makes the four golden signals a first-class rule.
Avoids logging/tracing for its own sake and names specific production questions.
Includes privacy/cost caution for high-volume logs or high-cardinality labels.

evals.name: review-finds-stuck-job-risk
evals.prompt: Review this diff conceptually: it adds a jobs table with id, user_id, status default 'pending', and a worker that sets status='running' then calls an external API. It has three retries but no timeout fields or logs. What are the highest-risk issues?
evals.expected_output: The response uses severity-first review, flags missing work identity, stale pending/running recovery, external timeout, retry budget/backoff/jitter, observability, and tests before style concerns.

assertions.text: Leads with stuck states and unsafe retries as high-risk findings.
Mentions missing timeout, lease, heartbeat, stale detection, or terminal transition.
Does not focus primarily on formatting or naming style.

evals.name: negative-pure-ui-mockup
evals.prompt: Make the hero section typography on this static marketing page feel more premium. There is no backend, no form, no runtime behavior, and no analytics request in scope.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not push queue, retry, distributed-system, or observability architecture into a purely visual static page request.

assertions.text: Does not introduce background jobs, idempotency tables, retries, or observability architecture.

evals.name: passive-dependency-boundaries
evals.prompt: Add retry handling to src/payments/charge.ts. It currently constructs a PaymentClient inside chargeCustomer(), reads PAYMENT_TIMEOUT_MS from the environment, and uses Date.now() for audit metadata. Keep the change easy to test and add whatever tests make sense.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads maintainable-code passively, reads nearby construction and test patterns, makes the payment client, config, and clock replaceable through local idioms, adds focused tests with stubs/fakes for success and retry failure paths, and keeps production wiring straightforward.

assertions.text: Makes hard dependencies explicit without a broad dependency injection rewrite
Tests can simulate payment success, retryable failure, and non-retryable failure without a real payment service
Runs or identifies focused tests/typechecks

evals.name: boundary-refactor-edge-case
evals.prompt: This order fulfillment function is impossible to unit test. It validates inventory, calls our warehouse SDK, writes to Postgres, publishes an event, and formats the HTTP response. Refactor it without turning the code into interface soup.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/dependency-boundaries.md, preserves behavior, separates framework response formatting from policy, introduces narrow replacement points for warehouse, database, and event publishing, avoids unnecessary interfaces, and adds tests with suitable fakes or stubs.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/dependency-boundaries.md
Does not add interfaces for every class or helper
Includes a strategy for contract or integration coverage around external adapters

evals.name: test-double-choice
evals.prompt: I need tests for a notification workflow. It sends one email, writes an audit record, and enqueues a follow-up job. Should I mock all three dependencies or use fakes?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/test-doubles.md and recommends the least powerful doubles that prove behavior: a capturing email sender or spy for the email interaction, an in-memory audit repository fake, and a fake or captured job queue, with contract coverage for risky adapters.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/test-doubles.md
Chooses doubles based on behavior and interaction risk, not a blanket mocking rule
Mentions adapter or contract coverage where mocks/fakes could drift

evals.name: review-testability-priority
evals.prompt: Review this PR for testability. The diff adds a static FraudService.getInstance(), calls fetch() inside the pricing rules, reads System.getenv() in three methods, and replaces a behavior test with strict mock call ordering.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/review-rubric.md, leads with high-impact findings about hidden globals and side effects in policy code, explains how the strict mock ordering makes tests brittle, and proposes narrow repair directions with verification notes.

assertions.text: Agent reads references/review-rubric.md
Findings are ordered by testability and safety impact rather than style preference
Review cites concrete hidden dependency and brittle test risks
